story.thesis: The AI Act's high-risk deadlines moved by 12 to 16 months, but nothing was repealed: re-plan the compliance roadmap, don't pause it.
story.audience: Leadership and compliance teams of companies that use AI in the EU
story.ask: Re-plan the roadmap to the new dates this quarter

parts.title: The new calendar
parts.desc: What moved and by how much

slides.kicker: Briefing for leadership and compliance teams
slides.title: The AI Act, re-timed
slides.subtitle: What the Digital Omnibus on AI changed, what it left alone, and what to do this quarter.
slides.notes: Open with the one-line takeaway: nothing in the AI Act was repealed, but the clock for high-risk systems moved. Everything on screen is sourced on the last slide.
Walk through the parts quickly. Click any line to jump to it.

slides.title: Nothing was repealed. The clock moved.
slides.text: The Digital Omnibus on AI amends the AI Act. It entered into force on 27 July 2026, days before the original high-risk deadline.
slides.notes: Political agreement came on 6 May 2026. The regulation was adopted on 8 July, published on 24 July and entered into force on 27 July 2026.

slides.title: One regulation, adopted and in force within three weeks

tiles.label: In force, three days after publication

slides.notes: Three weeks from adoption to entry into force. The speed matters: it landed just before the original 2 August 2026 deadline.

slides.caption: Extra time for stand-alone high-risk systems (Annex III).
slides.title: High-risk systems gained more than a year

bullets.title: Annex III
bullets.text: 2 Aug 2026 → 2 Dec 2027 (hiring, credit scoring, public services)

bullets.title: Article 50(2)
bullets.text: marking duty: four more months for systems already on the market

slides.notes: Annex III is the big one for most organisations: hiring tools, credit scoring, access to public services. Annex I covers AI built into regulated products.

slides.title: Two dates moved; the rest of the schedule still stands
slides.notes: Start on 'Original schedule', then switch to 'After the Omnibus' and let the room see which dates move. Filled dots already apply.

slides.title: Three duties already apply while the high-risk clock restarts
slides.notes: Same dates, read as ranges. Dashed boxes show where the old deadline sat. The dotted line is the Omnibus entering into force on 27 July 2026.

slides.title: Four smaller changes reach beyond the deadlines

items.title: Marking
items.text: Generative systems already on the market have until 2 Dec 2026 to mark AI-generated content.

items.title: New prohibitions
items.text: Article 5 now bans non-consensual intimate images of real people and child sexual abuse material.

items.title: AI literacy
items.text: Article 4 now asks organisations to support staff AI literacy, not to ensure a set level.

items.title: Small mid-caps
items.text: A new category of company gets simplifications that were reserved for SMEs.

slides.source: Sources: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744; Gibson Dunn and Orrick report the new bans apply from 2 Dec 2026.
slides.notes: One sentence per change. Small mid-caps are defined in Recommendation (EU) 2025/1099.

slides.title: The Omnibus is not a pause
slides.text: Three sets of duties already apply. The risk-based structure of the AI Act stays; what moved is when parts of it apply.
slides.notes: This is the slide that stops people from reading the Omnibus as a delay of everything.

slides.title: A bank builds a new credit-scoring model. From when do the high-risk requirements apply?

options.why: That was the original date. The Omnibus moved Annex III to 2 December 2027.
Creditworthiness assessment is an Annex III use, so the new date is 2 December 2027.
That is the new date for Annex I: AI built into regulated products.

slides.notes: Ask the room to vote with hands before you click the answer they chose.

slides.title: Six checks to finish before year end
items: List every AI system in use and mark which fall under Annex III or Annex I.
Re-plan the roadmap to 2 Dec 2027 and 2 Aug 2028, without pausing it.
If you provide generative tools already on the market, meet the marking duty by 2 Dec 2026.
Check content-generation features against the new Article 5 bans.
Keep the staff AI-literacy programme running.
Check whether the company qualifies as a small mid-cap.
slides.note: Suggested actions, not legal advice. Tick them live with the team that owns each one.
slides.notes: Tick each item with its owner in the room.
